candidates.observable: When the next operator disclosure leaves a third-party AI vendor unnamed, before 2027-11-01: that vendor's own public channel (framework update, model card, postmortem, or safety report) names or clearly references the same incident within 60 days of the operator's disclosure. If no vendor-side reference surfaces within 60 days for any such incident by 2027-11-01, that counts as the claim failing for that incident rather than as inconclusive.
candidates.switch_off: Without frontier AI there is no vendor bound by a safety-framework disclosure norm distinct from ordinary vendor contract confidentiality; an unnamed SaaS subprocessor in a breach notice has no independent public disclosure channel that names itself on a separate schedule.
candidates.rival: Any unnamed vendor eventually surfaces through ordinary trade press digging, unrelated to whether it publishes its own framework-driven disclosures.
candidates.region: what stays unknown · the shape of the redaction

candidates.title: An acknowledged-but-undated monitoring gap at one incident gets a date only once a second incident at the same operator forces it
candidates.mechanism: An operator that discloses 'we did not have visibility during period X' without dating the start of X leaves it undated in that disclosure, but a subsequent, unrelated incident at the same operator that requires reconstructing a timeline produces a dated boundary for the earlier gap as a byproduct, because the second investigation's own evidentiary needs force a date the first disclosure had no obligation to supply.
candidates.observable: When an operator that has disclosed an undated monitoring gap has a second agentic incident disclosed before 2027-12-01: the second disclosure's materials (report, filing, or timeline) supply a start date for the first gap that the first disclosure did not state. If no operator with a prior undated monitoring-gap disclosure has a second disclosed incident by 2027-12-01, that counts as evidence of non-occurrence of a qualifying second incident rather than evidence against the mechanism, since no test case would yet exist.
candidates.switch_off: Without frontier AI there is no 'monitoring gap' category distinct from ordinary logging retention; a conventional IT incident's visibility gap is a retention-policy fact stated once, not a recurring category an operator has reason to leave undated across separate agent-monitoring disclosures.
candidates.rival: Any two incidents at the same company naturally accumulate more total disclosed detail over time as journalists and regulators ask more questions, independent of any specific gap-dating mechanism.
candidates.region: what stays unknown · the shape of the redaction

candidates.title: A regulator's anonymized aggregate incident report reproduces the same dark categories the individual operator disclosures left dark
candidates.mechanism: When a regulator publishes an aggregate or anonymized summary built from individual operator incident reports, the categories absent from the aggregate (cost bands, model-identity classes, third-party-involvement rates) mirror the categories individual operators declined to state, because the regulator's aggregate cannot report what the underlying filings did not contain, regardless of the aggregation and anonymization step.
candidates.observable: When the first regulator-published aggregate report drawing on operator-submitted AI agentic-incident filings is released, before 2028-03-01: the categories it omits or reports only as 'not consistently available' include at least two of {cost, internal model identity, third-party identity, severity-threshold status} — the same categories individual operator disclosures in the same period left dark. If no such regulator aggregate report is published by 2028-03-01, that counts as evidence that no qualifying mandatory-reporting regime had produced a public aggregate yet, not evidence against the mirroring claim.
candidates.switch_off: Without frontier AI there is no agentic-incident-specific mandatory filing regime whose aggregate would mirror individual redactions; general breach-notification aggregates (e.g. state AG summaries) already aggregate an unrelated, long-established category set, so this is not merely 'regulators redact too.'
candidates.rival: Regulatory aggregates are always thin on specifics because agencies deliberately coarsen any data release for privacy, independent of what the underlying filings actually contained.
candidates.region: what stays unknown · the shape of the redaction

candidates.title: The categories a disclosed incident leaves dark predict which category a follow-on probe against the same operator targets first
candidates.mechanism: A published incident disclosure's redaction pattern is legible to an outside prober as a map of what the operator has not verified or instrumented (an undated monitoring gap implies detection latency; an unnamed internal model implies unpublished model inventory); a follow-on intrusion attempt or red-team probe against the same operator concentrates on the surface the redaction pattern implies is weakest, before any inside information changes hands.
candidates.observable: When a publicly reported follow-on security probe or disclosed intrusion attempt targets an operator within 12 months after that operator's own agentic-incident disclosure left the monitoring-gap timing or internal-model-identity category dark, before 2028-01-01: the follow-on probe's targeted surface matches the category the prior disclosure left dark, in a majority of qualifying probe-disclosure pairs found. If fewer than two qualifying follow-on probes against previously-disclosing operators are publicly reported by 2028-01-01, that counts as evidence of non-disclosure of follow-on probes rather than evidence the targeting pattern does not hold.
candidates.switch_off: Without frontier AI there is no 'undated monitoring gap' or 'unnamed internal model' category for a redaction pattern to expose; a conventional breach's redacted fields (which server, which credential) do not map onto a distinct AI-deployment attack surface a prober would target differently than a generic system.
candidates.rival: Attackers always target whatever surface is easiest regardless of any prior operator disclosure, since public disclosures are read by defenders far more than by the specific attacker planning the next probe.
candidates.region: what stays unknown · the shape of the redaction
